**Finding: MISSING (critical) — no indemnification provision in the Agreement.**

The document jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability). Section 20 is entirely absent, yet four separate clauses assume an indemnity exists:

- **§ 9.3** — termination right depends on "the remedies required by Section 20.5" (a clause that does not exist)
- **§ 19.4** — carves out "indemnified claims" from the exclusive warranty remedy
- **§ 21.3** — Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"
- **§ 30.5** — preserves rights of "an indemnified party" and "vested indemnity rights"

With no Vendor IP indemnity at all, this falls into the rule's walk-away category, so I drafted to the preferred position rather than the fallback.

**Redline inserted (validated ok:true)** — new Section 20 after § 19.5:

- **20.1** Vendor defends/indemnifies Customer and Affiliates for (a) IP infringement by Services, Deliverables or Vendor Technology, (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, (c) unauthorized access to Customer Data caused by Vendor, (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct
- **20.2** Customary exclusions (unauthorized Customer modification, combination, Customer specifications)
- **20.3** Standard notice / control / cooperation procedure, with consent required for settlements imposing non-monetary obligations on the indemnified party
- **20.4** Narrow Customer indemnity — Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law only, and expressly the sole Customer indemnity
- **20.5** Procure / modify / replace / refund IP remedies, restoring the clause already cross-referenced by § 9.3

No super-cap was proposed, since § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims outside the liability cap — raising it would re-trade a term that already favours us.
